subject: Throughput saturation protocol and noise-modeling — test deliverables
messages:
From: benchmarking-team@velox.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: ethan.price@globex.com
Date: 2026-08-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Velox RFP: clarifications on throughput/latency characterization

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP intake. A few follow-ups from our side — for the performance questionnaire we'd like a succinct protocol that covers:

- The exact testbed configuration you will use (GPU type, batcher settings, network topology)
- Synthetic traffic shapes and how you'll model burst/diurnal noise
- Measurement method for tail latency (p95/p99/p999) and how you will exclude warm-up behavior
- How you validate graceful degradation (fallback to model-variant or queued requests) under saturation
- Deliverables: raw trace logs, aggregated percentile tables, kernel-level timings if available

We want to understand both the steady-state throughput envelope and the saturation/failure modes. Can you commit to sharing the test plan and a sample of anonymized traces? Also please include any constraints (max sequence length, tokenization differences) we should be aware of.

Best,
Velox Benchmarking Team
(benchmarking-team@velox.ai)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: benchmarking-team@velox.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velox RFP: clarifications on throughput/latency characterization

Hi — thanks for the clear list. Below is our proposed test protocol and a short mapping of what we will deliver. Attaching the detailed YAML test plan and a sample noise model CSV.

Executive summary (what we will measure)
- Steady-state throughput envelope (QPS) for target percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) across sequence lengths (32/128/512).
- Saturation curve (throughput vs offered load) and inflection point where tail latency degrades > 2x baseline.
- Graceful degradation proof: behavior when capacity is constrained (we exercise model-variant fallback and regional spillover).
- Cold-start contribution to tails (measure cold vs warm request latencies and provide deconvolution).

Testbed configuration
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB (driver and CUDA versions listed in YAML). We will also run a representative quantized variant on T4 for cost-performance comparison (same model weights, different kernels).
- Networking: colocated RDMA-enabled hosts for the primary runs; additional runs over 10GbE to show network sensitivity.
- Software: Redwood serving runtime v2.3.1, kernel selection heuristics enabled, batching engine configured per-profile (dynamic continuous batching with max_batch_size=64, target_latency_ms=50).
- Model settings: sequence lengths 32/128/512; temperature/decoding deterministic for throughput runs; kv-cache warm strategy documented in plan.

Traffic and noise modeling
- Base traffic shapes: constant QPS plateau, sinusoidal diurnal, and Poisson spike bursts (modeled with 200ms-1s burst windows).
- We add controlled background noise: 5-15% randomized long-latency requests to emulate upstream dependency variance. Noise model samples included in attached CSV.
- For burst tests we vary offer points from 10% to 300% of nominal capacity in 10% increments and hold each for 60s to measure steady tails.

Measurement methodology
- Sampling: all requests are uniquely traced (trace-id); we will publish aggregated percentiles and also provide the raw time-series (per-second counts, per-request latencies).
- Tail reporting: p99.9 included for short windows (10s) and longer windows (5m) to differentiate microbursts vs sustained degrade.
- Warm-up exclusion: first 120s of each run are considered warm-up and excluded from steady-state aggregates; cold-start tests are run separately with single-shot replica starts.
- Decomposition: we will provide a breakdown of time spent in (a) queuing, (b) model-kernel execution, (c) I/O (network/serialization), and (d) cache-miss penalties (kv-cache miss latency). Kernel-level timing availability depends on GPU profiling capture; where available we will provide a per-layer timing CSV.

Graceful degradation scenarios
- Model-variant fallback: configure routing policy to fallback to a smaller quantized model when per-replica queue size exceeds threshold; we will quantify drop in output quality (via a short eval set) vs latency gains.
- Regional spillover: if primary region saturated, we will route a subset to a secondary region (measured separately) and provide end-to-end latency deltas.

Deliverables and cadence
- Within 5 business days: detailed test plan YAML (attached) + noise model sample.
- After tests (2-3 days run + analyze): aggregated percentile tables (CSV), raw traces (gzipped), per-run config manifests, and kernel timing CSVs where possible.
- Post-run summary: a 1-page executive brief showing capacity envelope, saturation inflection, and recommended configuration knobs (batching, max-seq, fallback thresholds) for your production workload.

Constraints and notes
- Max request size for the primary model: 1024 tokens; we will not exceed this without explicit permission.
- Deterministic decoding for throughput runs; quality-related metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic eval) can be provided in a separate quality pass.
- We will anonymize payloads in published traces per your compliance note.

Next steps
- Let us know if the three sequence lengths are sufficient or if you want a custom distribution.
- Confirm whether you want T4 quantized runs included in the initial deliverables or as a follow-up.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
